//: Why this file exists: its mere presence makes VS Code's chat host detect this plugin as the 'Open Plugin' format.
The host has a hard-coded format table; its detector picks the format by which manifest file is present:
'.plugin/plugin.json' present       -> Open Plugin format  (token '${PLUGIN_ROOT}', env var PLUGIN_ROOT)
otherwise                            -> legacy Copilot format (NO token expansion at all)
Open Plugin is the only format that expands '${PLUGIN_ROOT}' in our hook commands and injects PLUGIN_ROOT into the
hook process environment. If we shipped a bare 'plugin.json' instead, the host would pick the legacy Copilot format,
'${PLUGIN_ROOT}' in hooks/hooks.json would be left literal, and the hook command would point at a nonexistent path
and never run. So this manifest is required even though it carries no real content of its own.
The actual hook is in hooks/hooks.json, which the host auto-loads because this manifest declares no exclusive 'hooks.paths'.
Precedent: microsoft/GitHub-Copilot-for-Azure ships plugin/.plugin/plugin.json for exactly this reason.
name: csharp-dev-kit-skill-tracker
description: Tracks Copilot skill activations so the skill-usage feedback survey can be triggered. Only loaded while C# Dev Kit is active (chatPlugins 'when' gate). The PostToolUse hook lives in hooks/hooks.json.
